quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, you should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to entering traffic.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Stop in the middle of the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic light. Traffic moves counterclockwise around a center island. Enter from the right and yield to cars already in the roundabout. Follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: You come to a blocked intersection. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Use your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side. Wait until the road ahead is clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: An intersection has no signs or signals. You and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time. You should:

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signals, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Yield to them first, then you can go.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other traffic is near.
Signal only if you see other traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other traffic is near.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from the curb. Make this a habit so you follow the law every time.

questions.question: The crossing signals at a railroad are flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When crossing signals flash, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Look and listen for an oncoming train. Watch for lowered crossing gates or approaching trains.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal. Check for other drivers also moving into your lane.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your driving. If you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress lowers your focus on the road. Wait to drive if you are feeling emotionally unstable.

questions.question: When passing a parked vehicle, you should:

options.text: Be ready for someone to step out or a car to pull out suddenly.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Honk to alert people to your presence.
Speed up to avoid pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for someone to step out or a car to pull out suddenly.
questions.explanation: Leave space between your vehicle and parked cars. Someone may open a door and step out, or a parked car may suddenly pull into traffic.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle is coming at you head-on in your lane, honk your horn to get their attention. If they don't move, steer to the right to escape. Don't steer left because the other driver might correct at the last moment and you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.
Make sure your tires are filled to the correct pressure.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, check that your tires have good tread and are filled to the right pressure. Slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive at the same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when some drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive at the same speed as the traffic around you, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. This means:

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the edge of the road marks the boundary between the travel lane and the shoulder. If the edge line angles toward the center of the road, the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to re-enter the main road after a stop, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you see them.
Move to the left lane.
Yield to them.
Speed up to pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to them.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to pull back onto the main road after stopping to pick up or drop off passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely re-enter traffic.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: You have done all you need to do.
Stay until the police arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.
You can leave right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection when the traffic light turns solid yellow. You should:

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light at an intersection, slow down and stop before entering if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: When you see a '45 mph where workers present' sign, you should:

options.text: Slow down right away.
Drive at a safe speed for the conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less when workers are present.
Move to the right lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed for the conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less when workers are present.
questions.explanation: In a work zone with an advisory speed for workers, you must slow down to protect workers but can drive at the normal speed limit when workers are not present. Watch for workers and slow down if you see them.

questions.question: The posted speed limit shows:

options.text: Only a recommended speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed when conditions are ideal.
The maximum safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit. When conditions are poor, slow down.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:

options.text: Make both effects weaker.
Make both effects stronger.
Help cure an illness.
Improve your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make both effects stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both effects stronger. Driving after consuming alcohol or drugs is dangerous. Driving after mixing them is even more dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Divided highway ends.
One-way traffic ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Keep to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to pass safely. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep hill ahead.

questions.question: When another driver is passing your car, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them return to your lane safely.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your signal.
questions.explanation: Signal three to four seconds before you turn.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to allow them to merge safely.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means you can pass if it is safe. Only pass if oncoming traffic is clear.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. This is:

options.text: Only necessary if other cars are nearby.
A good habit and required by law.
Only necessary during the maneuver, not before.
Not necessary if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal your intention well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle right or left. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or back so the other driver can see your vehicle.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to clear a path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to clear a path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, you must slow down, clear a path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are difficult.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are difficult.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn of work on or near the road. Drive very carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is beginning.
You may see more pedestrians.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Obey the school zone speed limit during posted times. An "End school zone" sign marks the end of a reduced speed zone.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than the other cars.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when heavy rain makes it hard to see. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is so heavy you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching while you drive on a one-way street. You must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: When you approach a red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are crossing.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if no sign forbids it.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The fastest or slowest legal speed under dangerous conditions.
The fastest or slowest legal speed under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest or slowest legal speed under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or in bad weather. If conditions make the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Find a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell you a train might be coming. Obey all warning signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning sign.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a driver wants to pass. This creates space in front of your vehicle so they can pass more quickly and easily.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your wheels away from the curb.
Turn your wheels toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking on an uphill slope, turn your wheels away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll toward the curb, not into traffic.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They always know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They drive better because they are more careful.
They react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: A vehicle is entering the freeway from an entrance ramp into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass them.
Honk your horn to warn them.
Change lanes or slow down to give them room.
Do nothing because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to give them room.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. Change lanes when possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them to the right.
Turn them to the left.
Keep them straight ahead.
Leave the transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking on a downhill slope, turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls, it will move away from traffic.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Passing bad drivers to get ahead in traffic.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify dangers before they happen and take action to prevent accidents. It helps protect you from careless, aggressive, or impaired drivers.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react more slowly to dangers on the road.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to dangers on the road.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn when needed.
